correctness.rationale: For every integer N≥2, u=βe1+εe2 and v=εe3+γ∑e_j are orthonormal for ε=1/N, β²=1−ε², γ=β/√N. A=2I+uvᵀ+vuᵀ has eigenvalues 1,3 on span(u,v), 2 elsewhere, so is SPD of condition 3 and a single Arnoldi step from u gives v exactly. With disjoint column supports every full-rank two-row sketch must pick one of first two rows and one of next N+1; four row-amplitude types exhaust selection. Since β>γ>ε, all min-singular-value maximizers {1,j≥4} have sketch condition √N, whereas unique condition-minimizer {2,3} has condition one. DEIM and pivoted-QR Q-DEIM both pick the former. With orthonormal V, κ(VR^{-1})=κ(SV) for SV=QR. Independent exact rational tests covered selected N=2,3,9,100; symbolic four-type proof supplies uniform quantifier.
residual_risks: Exact arithmetic, unweighted row subsets, rank two; the tiny-amplitude condition-optimal pair is not asserted numerically stable.

value.rationale: PASS: The exact counterexample falsifies a natural surrogate-objective implication for a current deterministic Krylov selection strategy even when the parent SPD matrix is well conditioned, and the algorithm pivots exhibit the theoretically inferior selection. It is a motivated structural limitation of the chosen metric, not a recommendation to sample vanishing-amplitude rows in floating point.
